data.leadership_messages: Overall this control account appears to be well laid out with sound logic and dependencies where necessary. Durations will be checked based upon lower comments.

areas.text: IMP Alignment and Vertical Traceability: Assess whether the Integrated Master Plan (IMP) establishes a logical planning framework for organizing program accomplishments, planning objectives, and future IMS development.Strong- IMP is detailed to Schedule level 3, however, more detail will soon be necessary for detailed Acceptance CriteriaPlanning Structure and Task Definition Maturity: Assess whether the contractor has established a logical planning hierarchy and sufficiently defined planning tasks to support detailed IMS development.Strong- concurWorkflow, Dependencies, and Handoffs Logic: Assess whether the contractor has established a logical execution strategy that defines workflow, identifies dependencies, and clearly describes organizational interfaces.Strong- P6 draft shows full Predecessor and Successor planning for all work. Planning Constructs: Assess whether planning constructs provide a practical and repeatable framework for organizing work and supporting future IMS development.Strong- concurDuration and Assumption Basis: Assess whether planned durations are supported by reasonable assumptions and documented planning rationale.Mod- actual dates are not reflective of final schedule, which is expected at this time. It seems the durations for each work item is approx. 6 weeks which may or may not be accurate.Quantity-Based Data (QBD): Assess whether objective quantities and production rates support the planned durations.N/A

Interface Identification: Assess whether key technical, schedule, organizational, and supplier interfaces have been identified and documented.Strong – Integration efforts are called out within the line items and logic is present.Dependency Management: Assess whether execution dependencies between product elements are identified, understood, and incorporated into planning.Strong- Full list of predecessors and successors are present and visible.Cross-Product/Cross-Function Schedule Alignment: Assess whether cross-product/cross-function schedules are logically aligned to support integrated program execution.Strong - Line items denote linkage where applicable to other functional areas.Roles, Responsibilities, and Coordination: Assess whether responsibilities for managing cross-product/cross-function integration are clearly assigned and consistently executed.Strong – Connections and responsibilities are known to CAM and have been discussed. Integration Risk and Follow-up: Assess whether unresolved integration issues are evaluated, prioritized, and managed to support continued planning maturity.N/A
